title: Irish crochet butterfly motif
excerpt: A delicate butterfly motif in lace weight yarn worked with Irish crochet raised techniques. Four wings radiate from a central body worked in trebles.
sourceNotes: An Irish crochet butterfly with two upper and two lower wings built over foundation arcs, with a padded treble body at the centre.

glossaryTerms.definition: The larger pair of wings in the butterfly motif, each worked over a longer chain arc with more trebles than the lower wings.
The central column of the butterfly, worked as a series of slip stitches or tight double crochets along a short foundation chain to form the thorax.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished motif approx. 7 cm wide x 5 cm tall.
crochet.finishedSizeText: One butterfly motif approx. 7 cm wide.

Chain 10. Work dc along the chain, then work 1 dc, 7 tr, 1 dc into each of two chain arcs to form the two upper wings. Join the wing tips with a slip stitch at the centre top.
Chain 7. Work 1 dc, 5 tr, 1 dc into each of two shorter arcs below the upper wings. Join at the centre bottom.
Work 8 dc tightly down the centre joining point to form the body. Attach two short chain loops (ch 6 each) at the top for the antennae. Fasten off and weave in all ends with the tapestry needle.
